causal_limits: 150 ms future-destructor observations plus finite 5 s backup do not prove native socket release, joined results or permanent leaks; listener rebind is a separate observation.
Fault wrappers are controlled inputs at actual established worker/listener I/O seams, not observed native OS failures. Disabled wrappers delegate the same concrete actual I/O.
CompletedPeerFailure is a distinct controlled typed result after an actual forwarded response and release handshake; it is not an H2 production error.
Typed missing-result checks precede downcasts; baseline failures at those checks cannot establish later exact-type assertions.
Poisoned actual log writer checks client failure first; typed observer cause is covered separately. Baseline poison recording may first fail on its erased string cause.
Final-send reset controls establish actual INTERNAL_ERROR independently, then require a non-I/O typed H2 error from the real final-send branch; private User kind is not directly exposed.
Flow-control release, capacity and other inherited ignored failures remain source-only branches without a dedicated causal control; no blanket suppression or support claim.
Early prerequisite failures fail the controls; correct complete baseline ownership is intentionally not implemented. Raw tasks can remain until runtime drop on unexpected setup exits.
All broad lifecycle defects are retained. Imported parser/deadline/oracle fixes are already separately signed and source approved; their final runtime verification is root-owned.
